articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Native Multimodal Reasoning and Extended Context
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5, featuring natively fused vision, audio, and text reasoning in a single architecture rather than bolted-on adapters. The model demonstrates significant gains on doctoral-level science benchmarks and supports a 1-million-token context window, enabling full-codebase and book-length analysis in a single pass.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves Gold Medal Performance on International Math Olympiad 2026
articles.summary: DeepMind announced that Gemini Ultra 2 scored 35 out of 42 on this year's IMO problem set, surpassing the gold-medal threshold and outperforming all but a handful of human contestants. The result was verified by independent mathematicians and represents a step change over last year's near-miss results, raising questions about the remaining gaps between AI and elite human mathematical creativity.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Begins Commercial Deployment of Figure 03 Humanoid in BMW Plants
articles.summary: Figure's third-generation humanoid robot has entered series production deployment at two BMW manufacturing facilities in South Carolina, performing bin-picking, part transfer, and quality inspection tasks alongside human workers. The robots leverage on-board vision-language models to interpret natural-language instructions from floor supervisors, reducing retooling time for new tasks from days to minutes.

articles.title: Meta Releases Open-Source Llama 4 Behemoth with 288B Active Parameters Under Permissive License
articles.summary: Meta publicly released the full weights of Llama 4 Behemoth, a mixture-of-experts model with 288 billion active parameters and nearly 2 trillion total parameters, under a revised open-source license that permits commercial use. Early benchmarks show it competitive with proprietary frontier models, and the release includes optimized quantized variants that run on a single 8×H100 node.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics Atlas Electric Demonstrates Autonomous Disaster Response at DARPA Exercise
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics showcased its all-electric Atlas robot completing a full DARPA-style disaster response course autonomously, including valve manipulation, rubble traversal, and casualty identification with zero human teleoperation. The demonstration used a new whole-body model-predictive controller that fuses LiDAR and stereo vision for real-time terrain adaptation, marking a major milestone in unstructured-environment locomotion.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm-Class N14 Process Node
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed initial volume production at its Fab 20 in Kaohsiung on the N14 process node, featuring gate-all-around nanosheet transistors with backside power delivery. The node offers a 15% speed improvement or 30% power reduction compared to N2, and is expected to power next-generation AI accelerators and mobile SoCs shipping in early 2027.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Clearance for Second-Generation Brain-Computer Interface Implant
articles.summary: The FDA granted de novo clearance to Neuralink's N2 implant, which doubles the electrode count to 2,048 channels and adds bidirectional stimulation capability. Early clinical trial participants with spinal cord injuries demonstrated full cursor and robotic arm control with sub-100ms latency, and the bidirectional feature opens a pathway toward sensory feedback restoration.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude 'Computer Use 2.0' Agent Framework for Enterprise Automation
articles.summary: Anthropic launched an upgraded computer-use agent framework that enables Claude to autonomously operate desktop and web applications through structured action primitives with built-in safety guardrails and audit logging. The system supports multi-step workflows across enterprise tools like SAP, Salesforce, and internal dashboards, and includes a human-in-the-loop approval tier configurable by risk level.
